name: Jorge da Costa
summary:
Dom Jorge da Costa (1450–1508) was a Portuguese cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church during the late Renaissance.

As a key figure in the Vatican, da Costa was instrumental in shaping the church's policies and relations with European monarchies. He was a strong advocate for the Counter-Reformation and worked tirelessly to promote the interests of the Catholic Church.

Da Costa's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped establish the Jesuit order and contributed to the development of the Catholic Church's diplomatic corps. His influence can be seen in the church's relations with European powers during the 16th century, and his reputation has endured through the centuries as a symbol of loyalty and dedication.
